items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: There was a fine English bass man backing us up

ctx.x: This was the pianist Jay McShann, and his personality sent me as soon as we were introduced. He, Charles Shavers, Buddy Tate, Albert Nicholas and I, did a public aduience T.V.show for the B.B.C. at Ronnie Scott's club. Jay played and sang some real gone blues which knocked everybody out and when it came to accompanying me on my numbers, it was the first time I had been sent the way he sent me, in many moons. I have a tape of that session, thanks to an English jazz lover and friend of mine, named Leslie Parr, and…
There was a fine English bass man backing us up but the drummer was a little too modern and ligjt for our style.

It was October 27th when we did the T.V.show and the 28th was the concert at Odean - Hammersmith Theatre, which I later heard was the best night of the festival. The 29th I went to Bristol where I played at the Old Granary, which was a club owned by Acker Bilk. The band was from somewhere near Bristol, and we didn't rehears anything but we had a nice jam session the whole evening. Lily and I came back home the 2nd of November, happy as usual, with our visit to England.
